concerns.text: Task T015 (Compute Descriptors) lists a dependency on T019 (Filtering), but T019 itself depends on T013 (Download). The logical flow is T013 -> T019 -> T015. However, T015 is also listed as a dependency for T016 and T018. The current ordering in the text implies T015 runs after T019, but the 'Dependency' note in T015 says 'Must be completed after T014 (GB Builder) and T019'. This is semantically correct, BUT T019 is marked [B] (Blocking) and T015 is not. If T019 fails (e.g., no configs), T015 cannot run. The dependency chain is valid, but the 'Parallel' note in T018 ('Can run in parallel with T017c') is risky if T017c (Simulation) depends on T019 (Filtering) which depends on T015? No, T017c depends on T019. T018 depends on T015. T015 depends on T019. So T018 cannot run until T015 is done, which waits for T019. T017c also waits for T019. So T018 and T017c can run in parallel *after* T019 and T015 are done. The text says 'Can run in parallel with T017c' for T018, which is true *after* T015. But T015 depends on T019. The dependency chain is: T013 -> T019 -> T015 -> T018. T013 -> T019 -> T017c. So T018 and T017c are parallel *after* T015 and T019. The text is slightly ambiguous but the dependency graph holds. However, T017a-1 (Download Potentials) is marked [B] and depends on T017a-0. T017c depends on T017a-1. T017a (Perturbation logic) depends on T014. T017b (Engine) depends on T017a. T017c depends on T017a, T017b, T017a-1, T019. This is a deep dependency chain. The main issue is T019 is listed as a dependency for T015, but T019 is a filtering step that logically should happen *before* descriptor calculation to avoid wasting compute on invalid configs. The order T013 -> T019 -> T015 is correct. The concern is the [P] tag on T015. T015 depends on T019. T019 is [B]. So T015 cannot be [P] if it depends on a [B] task that might block the whole phase. The [P] tag implies it can run in parallel with other tasks, but it is blocked by T019. This is a semantic violation of the [P] definition.

Task T017a-1 (Download Potentials) is marked [B] and depends on T017a-0. It is a prerequisite for T017c. However, T017a (Perturbation logic) and T017b (Engine) are defined *before* T017a-1 in the list, but T017c depends on T017a-1. The logical flow for the simulation engine is: Define Logic (T017a) -> Implement Engine (T017b) -> Download Potentials (T017a-1) -> Run Simulation (T017c). The current order in the document lists T017a-1 *after* T017a and T017b, which is fine for implementation order, but the dependency for T017c is correct. The issue is T017a-1 is marked [B] (Blocking) but it is a data download task. If the download fails, the whole simulation phase blocks. This is correct behavior. The concern is the [P] tag on T017a and T017b. T017a depends on T014. T017b depends on T017a. T017a-1 depends on T017a-0. T017c depends on T017a, T017b, T017a-1, T019. T017a and T017b can be implemented in parallel with T017a-1? No, T017b depends on T017a. T017a-1 is independent of T017a/b. So T017a-1 can run in parallel with T017a/b. But T017a-1 is marked [B]. This is a contradiction. A [B] task should not be parallel with other tasks in the same phase if it blocks the final execution. The [B] tag is appropriate for T017a-1 because it blocks T017c. But the [P] tag on T017a and T017b is correct. The issue is the ordering of T017a-1 in the list. It is listed after T017a and T017b, which is fine. The concern is the [P] tag on T017a-1? No, T017a-1 is [B]. The concern is the [P] tag on T017a and T017b. They are [P] but they depend on T014. T014 is [P]. So T017a and T017b can run in parallel with T014? No, T017a depends on T014. So T017a cannot run until T014 is done. The [P] tag on T017a is incorrect if it depends on T014. The [P] tag means 'Can run in parallel' with other tasks, but it cannot run until T014 is done. This is a semantic violation. The [P] tag should only be used for tasks that have no dependencies on other tasks in the same phase or that are independent of the blocking chain. T017a depends on T014, so it cannot be [P] if T014 is not yet done. The [P] tag is misleading.

Task T016 (Alloy System Tagging) is marked [P] and depends on T015. T015 depends on T019. T019 depends on T013. T013 is [P]. The dependency chain is valid. However, T016 is listed as 'Can run in parallel with T018 ONLY after T014 is complete'. T018 depends on T015. T016 depends on T015. So T016 and T018 can run in parallel after T015. The text says 'ONLY after T014 is complete', but T015 depends on T014. So the condition 'after T014' is implied by 'after T015'. The text is redundant but not incorrect. The concern is the [P] tag on T016. T016 depends on T015. T015 is not [P] (it depends on T019 which is [B]). So T016 cannot be [P] if it depends on a non-[P] task. The [P] tag is semantically incorrect.
